title: Browse: concept/prerequisite navigation + search + graded-feedback UI
context: open-coding-curriculum is an open CC-BY (prose) / MIT (code) curriculum of beginner programming lessons with graded, runnable exercises across languages. Every exercise carries a reference solution proven correct in CI (solutionVerified:true), learner code runs zero-install in-browser via WASM, and all content is machine-readable structured data so third parties can build on it. The project targets absolute beginners — self-learners, public-library patrons, under-resourced school students, career-changers — and operates under a donated-compute lane with no server-side execution of learner code and no partner confirmed yet (verifiedNeed:false). A flat list of lessons is not enough — learners need to find where to start, see what they can unlock next, and get useful feedback when they fail an exercise. The navigation, search, and graded-feedback UI turn the corpus from a list of files into a learning experience.
objective: Add concept/prerequisite-driven navigation using the graph from occ-data-105, a search feature over lessons and concepts, and an improved graded-feedback UI that shows actionable hints and failure diagnostics after an exercise attempt.
acceptanceCriteria: Learner can navigate the concept/prerequisite graph: each lesson shows its prerequisites and the lessons it unlocks.
Search over lesson titles, concepts, and glossary terms is functional and returns ranked results.
Graded feedback UI shows: pass/fail status, which test cases failed and why (actionable diagnostics), and the first unused hint on failure.
Navigation and search are keyboard-accessible and screen-reader-usable.
pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint pass.
output: A merged PR adding concept/prerequisite navigation, search, and improved graded-feedback UI to the learner site.
